newsitem.title: GERMANY: German job office says budget top-up may be needed.
newsitem.headline: German job office says budget top-up may be needed.

text.p: The head of Germany's Federal Labour Office said on Thursday higher-than-expected unemployment this year could mean his organisation might need nearly seven billion marks ($4.1 billion) more funds this year.

Meeting regional labour office officials in the eastern town of Dresden, Federal Labour Office President Bernhard Jagoda said he expected unemployment to average at between 4.15 and 4.20 million this year.
That compared to the 3.95 million average on which the labour office's 1997 budget was based.
Jagoda said each additional 100,000 of unemployed meant some three billion marks in unemployment benefit pay-outs and 320 million marks in lost unemployment insurance revenues for the office.
Calcuated thus, that would mean extra costs of some 6.6 billion marks for a German government that has been looking at cutting labour office grants in the run-up to European monetary union.
